text: A servant took my horse, and another, who walked silently, led me through many dark and winding passages to the room of his master. <break time="0.8s" /> Never had a man changed so terribly in so short a time, and I could hardly believe that this pale figure was my old friend. <break time="0.8s" /> His skin was deathly pale, and his eyes shone with a strange light, his silky hair floating wildly around his face like a web. <break time="0.8s" /> He suffered from a sickness of the senses, so that only the plainest food and the softest clothes were bearable to him. <break time="0.8s" /> The scent of every flower troubled him, even faint light hurt his eyes, and only a few sounds from stringed instruments did not fill him with horror. <break time="0.8s" /> I shall perish in this terrible folly, he said, for I fear not danger itself, but the feeling of terror that it brings. <break time="0.8s" /> He also told me about his beloved sister, the Lady Madeline, his only companion for many years, whose long illness had puzzled her doctors. <break time="0.8s" /> While he was speaking, she passed slowly through a distant part of the room, and, without having noticed me, she disappeared. <break time="0.8s" /> That very evening she gave in to her illness, and I learned that I would probably never see her alive again.
